I grow maize on my only plot of land, intercropped with pigeon pea so that even if the maize does poorly we still have something to eat. I will plant the improved seed and apply the fertilizer I received through the FISP program this year—about two bags in total—because without it the soil here in Mangochi gives very little back. We depend entirely on the rains God provides, so I cannot irrigate, and I have no money for pesticides or manure from livestock. My children and I will do most of the work ourselves, but I will need to hire a few days of ganyu labor when the weeds are heavy and during harvest time.
